answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network maps interaction graphs into topological cut verifications. Agents partition clusters across a connectivity ridge where cross-partition transactions require game-theoretic multi-agent auditing. Colluding nodes that anchor synthetic identities like a static wharf cannot bridge independent clusters without locking collateral. When an audit detects forged cut bottlenecks, strict stake slashing dissolves malicious nodes like brittle shale, imposing superlinear attacker cost scaling with network diameter.
